class="markdown-body" data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">Several values are available as AMP macros that it is not currently possible to use as set targeting values.</p>
<p dir="auto">PAGEVIEWID - pageViewId<br>
HREF - equivalent to window.context.location.href<br>
ATTR(height) - Height attribute of the amp-ad element<br>
ATTR(width) - Width attribute of the amp-ad element<br>
ATTR(data-slot) - data-slot attribute of the amp-ad element<br>
ATTR(data-multi-size) - data-multi-size attribute of the amp-ad element<br>
ATTR(data-multi-size-validation) - data-multi-size-validation attribute of the amp-ad element<br>
ATTR(data-override-width) - data-override-width attribute of the amp-ad element<br>
ATTR(data-override-height) - data-override-height attribute of the amp-ad element<br>
ATTR(data-json) - data-json attribute of the amp-ad element<br>
ADCID - adClientId<br>
TGT - Just the targeting piece of data-json<br>
CANONICAL_URL - The canonical URL of the page.<br>
TIMEOUT - The publisher-specified timeout for the RTC callout.</p>
<p dir="auto">A possible strategy to set targeting to gam with one of these values is to pass one of them to prebid server and have prebid server include it in the response.</p>
<p dir="auto">What we would like to do is pass a pageviewid to gam so that we can associate impressions from the same pageview together on our gam log.</p></div></div><div data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">I would suggest we modify Brett's proposed solution to defining the custom keys from the AMP query string to look something like:<br>
<code class="notranslate">ext.prebid.adservertargeting:  [{ "key": "hb_ampparam", "source": "querystring", "value": "ampkey" }]</code></p>
<p dir="auto">Embedding the syntax in the request object implies we will load a copy of the amp query string parameters into the request JSON. Either we don't actually modify the request JSON this way, which could potentially confuse adapter authors, or we go through all that work on every case to support whatever corner case an adapter author can come up with for accessing that data. Given that even with this inclusion, the adapter cannot determine the original value in the request before it was overwritten by the querystring, nor even if it was set to begin with, I doubt there exists a case to include the query string values.</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap"></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></li><li <ol dir="auto">
<li>it's more generic, supporting future non-AMP, non-querystring interfaces</li>
<li>it's more consistent that Prebid Server core operates only the OpenRTB 'object of record'. I view the AMP 'module' to have just one job: convert the AMP query string to our canonical form.</li>
<li>copying AMP query string params to ext.prebid.amp.data is just a way to normalize the incoming request to our 'object of record', though I agree that adapters shouldn't have access to it. They only get data via the <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1I2eS40yMYJCgz8XvFljf4f59bEPsbWTrUpnD7a7uJEg/edit#" rel="nofollow">first party data</a> path. I've updated the proposal above to note removing ext.prebid.amp.data before sending to adapters.</li>
</ol></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap"></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></li><li In <a href="https://iabtechlab.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/OpenRTB-2-6_FINAL.pdf" rel="nofollow">this document,</a> please refer to paragraph 4.3.1 (format is the same for OpenRTB 2.5) - it describes fields in bidresponse.</p>
